final_recommendation: The room converged on a comprehensive trilateral package ready for Monday initialing: 70% RVC with three-year phase-in, bilateral labor panel with unannounced audits and automatic tariff remedies, Chapter 19 preserved for non-labor disputes, 3.6% phased dairy access in treaty text, and six-year review limited to labor/autos only. All parties explicitly committed to signing.
key_conflicts: Chapter 19 dispute settlement: Canada's non-negotiable red line vs. initial U.S. position to eliminate it entirely
Dairy market access: U.S. demand for Canadian supply-management concessions vs. Canada's domestic political constraints
Labor enforcement mechanism: need for binding remedies with treaty-text certainty vs. risk of post-signing regulatory dilution
key_concessions: U.S. accepted Chapter 19 for all non-labor disputes (retreating from initial position to kill it entirely)
Canada accepted 3.6% dairy market access phased over five years in binding treaty schedule
Mexico accepted automatic tariff suspension remedy for willful labor violations
All parties accepted six-year review limited to labor/autos only (not whole agreement)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement mechanism must remain (stated 'non-negotiable' and 'full stop')
U.S. Congress: labor panel authority must be in treaty text, not implementation regulations ('Congress will torch this' if watered down)
Auto/supply-chain: enforcement mechanism must have real-time audit authority and binding remedies, not 'phantom enforcement'
Dairy: 3.6% access must be in binding treaty schedule, not side letter
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation and compliance costs for manufacturers during three-year phase-in period
Political viability of dairy concessions in Canada's domestic ratification process
Operational details of unannounced audit logistics across three countries
Potential for six-year review to create recurring investment uncertainty despite limited scope
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional ratification timeline and political dynamics
Mexico's capacity to implement wage verification and union reform commitments
Supplier-level compliance costs and potential supply chain disruption during phase-in
Effectiveness of automatic tariff suspension as enforcement mechanism
Canadian domestic political reaction to dairy market access concession
uncertainty_notes: Specific operational procedures for unannounced audits remain undefined. The exact trigger threshold for 'willful violation' vs. inadvertent non-compliance was not specified. Timeline for Congressional ratification process not discussed. Potential interaction between six-year review and ongoing compliance investments unclear.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% vs 70% RVC with phase-in drove opening positions and required Mexico's bridge proposal to resolve; three-year phase-in became core element of final package
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor panel enforcement mechanism (unannounced audits, binding remedies, automatic tariff suspension) was central to U.S. Congress ratification support and drove treaty-text specificity demands throughout
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy access discussed as politically sensitive and required binding treaty schedule commitment, but did not block the deal—Canada accepted 3.6% phased access as part of broader package
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 'non-negotiable' and 'full stop'; U.S. concession to preserve it for non-labor disputes was decisive compromise enabling Canadian sign-on
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard sunset concern drove explicit shift to six-year review mechanism limited to labor/autos only, providing investment certainty that multiple parties cited as necessary for retooling commitments
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: U.S. Congress explicitly conditioned support on treaty-text enforcement language (not regulations), stating 'Congress will torch this' if diluted; drove USTR's commitment to lock details in treaty text
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Raised by auto/supply-chain representatives regarding retooling costs and compliance systems, but did not change the 70% RVC outcome—acknowledged as manageable with three-year phase-in
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico explicitly threatened bilateral U.S.-Mexico deal without Canada and imposed Monday deadline; this pressure drove Canada's acceptance of dairy concessions and package timeline

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
